questions.q: If momentum of a body is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo>%</mo></math>, then its kinetic energy increases by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
A body of mass m, moving with momentum p and kinetic energy K are related as follows,
K=p22m.
As the momentum of the body is increased by 20%, then its momentum becomes,
p+20100p=1.2 p
and the mass of the body remains unchanged. So, kinetic energy is directly related to the square of momentum. 

Hence, new kinetic energy K' will be,
K'=1.2 p22m

K'=1.44 K.

So, the percentage change in kinetic energy
=K'-KK×100 
=1.44K-KK×100
=1.44-1×100
=44%.

questions.q: Two bodies are having kinetic energies in the ratio 16:9. If they have same linear momentum, the ratio of their masses respectively is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy and the momentum of a moving object are related by

K=p22m   ...1

Hence, the ratio of the kinetic energies of two objects having masses m and m' can be calculated as follows:

KK'=p22mp22m'=m'm   ...2

Substitute the ratio of the kinetic energies into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the ratio of their masses.

⇒169=m'm⇒m:m'=9:16

questions.q: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi>MeV</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> collides with a hydrogen atom at rest. Soon after the collision, the particle comes to rest, and the atom recoils and goes to its first excited state. The initial kinetic energy of the particle (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>eV</mi></math>) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>N</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>.</mo></math> The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>N</mi></math> is: (Given the mass of the hydrogen atom to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>GeV</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>).........
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Given, M=200 MeV c-2 and m=1 GeV c-2, now use the concept of conservation of linear momentum, Mv0=mv⇒v=Mv0m  ...1.

Now use the conservation of energy, 

12Mv02=12mv2+∆E  ..2, here ∆E=13.6 eV, for the hydrogen atom in the ground state, now from equation, 1 & 2, 12Mv02=143∆E×108 eV=N4,

⇒N4=514 eV⇒N=51.

questions.q: A body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> collides head on elastically with a stationary body of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>. After collision, the smaller body reverses its direction of motion and moves with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. The initial speed of the smaller body before collision is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution:
Let u1 be the initial speed of the smaller body before collision. 

Let v be the final speed of the bigger body after collision.

Applying conservation of linear momentum,

1×u1+0=-2+3v⇒u1=-2+3v    ...1 

We know, coefficient of restitution for elastic perfectly collision is 1.

 ⇒1=v+2u1⇒v+2=u1    ...2 

Equating 1 and 2, we have

u1=4 m s-1.

questions.q: In a system two particles of masses $m_1=3 \mathrm{~kg}$ and $m_2=2 \mathrm{~kg}$ are placed at certain distance from each other. The particle of mass $m_1$ is moved towards the center of mass of the system through a distance $2 \mathrm{~cm}$. In order to keep the center of mass of the system at the original position, the particle of mass $m_2$ should move towards the center of mass by the distance _____ $\mathrm{cm}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta \mathrm{X}_{\text {C.O.M. }}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_1 \Delta \mathrm{x}_1+\mathrm{m}_2 \Delta \mathrm{x}_2}{\mathrm{~m}_1+\mathrm{m}_2} \\ & \Rightarrow 0=\frac{3 \times 2+2(-\mathrm{x})}{3+2} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{x}=3 \mathrm{~cm}\end{aligned}$
